verdict.rationale: Cloudflare Realtime is an SFU whose API lets you control which endpoints publish or receive audio, video, and data. Its docs describe a publish/subscribe model: subscribers pull remote tracks, and publications can exist with no subscriber. Community comments confirm that participants route through Cloudflare rather than peer-to-peer. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of per-track audio/video pull semantics (the pull example shown is for DataChannels), and hands-on corroboration that only subscribed tracks are forwarded to each participant.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, media routes through a selective forwarding unit or relay that delivers only the tracks each participant subscribes to

citations.quote: Use the Realtime SFU API to control which endpoints publish or receive audio, video, and data.
Traffic published into Cloudflare is free, including when no client subscribes to that publication.
When a subscriber pulls a remote DataChannel with `waitForAck: true`, the SFU holds delivery to that subscriber until it sends its first message (the acknowledgment).
